The scientific name derives from the Ancient Greek term for wickerwork, referring to the plants' habitus. The genus is named after Nicolas-Claude Fabri de Peiresc, a 16th-century French botanist.

Species may also be referred to as pincushion cacti, a common name which is also applied to other genera.

It is mixed into a hallucinogenic beverage called "Cimora" along with Trichocereus pachanoi.

Similar to the classification systems used for cellular organisms, virus classification is the subject of ongoing debate and proposals.  This is mainly due to the pseudo-living nature of viruses, which is to say they are non-living particles with some chemical characteristics similar to those of life.  As such, they do not fit neatly into the established biological classification system in place for cellular organisms.
